chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said:

Musa ibn Imran said: O my Lord! Admonish me. He said: I admonish you of Me. So he said: O my Lord! Admonish me. He said: I admonish you of Me -- three times. He said: O my Lord! Admonish me. He said: I admonish you of your mother. He said: O my Lord! Admonish me. He said: I admonish you of your mother. He said: O my Lord! Admonish me. He said: I admonish you of your father. He said: So it was said, because of that, that the mother has two-thirds of righteousness, and the father has one-third.

key_terms.أوصني: Awsini - admonish me, give me counsel
key_terms.البر: Al-Birr - righteousness, filial piety, good treatment of parents

ai.seo_question: Why does the mother receive two-thirds of righteousness in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) narrates a conversation between Prophet Musa (AS) and God. When Musa repeatedly asked for admonition, God first directed him to Himself three times (emphasizing devotion to God), then to his mother twice, and finally to his father once. The conclusion drawn is that the mother deserves two-thirds of a child's righteousness (birr) while the father deserves one-third, reflecting the mother's greater share of hardship in bearing and raising children.
